:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

II. $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ only if $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$.

III. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.
:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}&=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1}-2x_{2} &=0 \\ -2x_{2}-x_{3} &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{2}&=1 \\ x_{1}-2(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=2 \\ -2(1)-x_{3}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{3}=-2\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
2\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}-2\mathbf{a}_{3}=2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

Statement I is **false**. Statement II is **false**. Statement III is **false**.
